title: Scalar-extension local models of the integral root line
statement:
For the concrete Tate sheaves [def-pur-twist-sheaves], assume the completed Z_l root module has rank one. The integral tensor has a pro-etale unit trivialization. At every positive finite level its completed scalar reduction is the prescribed finite tensor, which has a unit trivialization and is nonzero if the base is nonempty. Local constancy, constructibility and finite stalks follow separately from the generic proved finite-line theorem. No derived assertion is included.

theorem purTwistIntegralLocalModels
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)]
    (hL : (purTwistZlModule S l).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1) :
    (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
      (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
      Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
      ∀ i, Nonempty ((purTwistIntegralModule S l E).over (U i) ≅
        (SheafOfModules.unit
          (WeilConjectures.completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E S)).over (U i))) ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ,
      Nonempty (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
        (WeilConjectures.completedIntegralCommRingProjectionUnrestricted l E S n)
          (purTwistIntegralModule S l E) ≅ purTwistFiniteOne S l E n) ∧
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
        (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
        ∀ i, Nonempty ((purTwistFiniteOne S l E n).over (U i) ≅
          (SheafOfModules.unit (WeilConjectures.integralCoefficientSheaf l E S n)).over (U i))) ∧
      (Nonempty S → ¬IsZero (purTwistFiniteOne S l E n))

proof.text: Use the sectionwise completed scalar pushout. Tensor base-change cancellation identifies the discrete integral tensor with the restriction of the completed scalar extension. The specified completed action makes the canonical map from that scalar extension linear; its restriction is the preceding tensor isomorphism, so it is invertible. Extract the rank-one local bases from the given finite locally free hypothesis and refine the covering sieve to a pro-etale precover. Extend these bases to obtain integral local unit models.

On every test object, identify discrete constant coefficients with continuous functions into the discrete valuation ring. The finite quotient map is surjective and has kernel generated by the positive uniformizer power. The inverse limit of these positive quotients is the adic completion. The kernel theorem for evaluation from a finitely generated adic completion identifies the completed projection kernel with the extension of that ideal. The two scalar reductions have the same universal property: a discrete-linear map to a finite-level module is completion-linear, since the projection kernel is generated by the discrete quotient kernel. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives the finite tensor comparison. Extend the integral local basis along each projection.

A positive uniformizer power generates a proper ideal in the coefficient DVR, so the finite quotient ring is nontrivial. A point on the nonempty base lifts to a member of the pro-etale covering family. On that member evaluation of continuous constant functions at this point shows that the finite coefficient sheaf has distinct zero and unit sections. The displayed local basis then prevents the finite twist from being a zero object.
